morphology_candidate.look_here_first: Start with young pubescence, leaf tips, and pistillate sepals: ochraceous young growth, consistently acute leaf tips, and sepal tips staying straight to slightly incurved are strong cues.
diagnostic_traits: ochraceous yellow-brown pubescence on young growth
pistillate sepals 7–8, yellowish woolly-tomentose, tips not recurved outward

confusers.separator: C. capitatus often has blunter/mucronate leaves and pistillate sepals whose tips flare or recurve outward.
C. lindheimerianus is generally lower and more dichotomously branched with smaller pistillate sepals and six terminal style segments.

diagnostic_image_needs: acute leaf tips and cordate bases

aliases: Croton capitatus var. lindheimeri (Engelm. & A.Gray) Müll.Arg.
taxonomy.notes: POWO and Flora of North America accept C. lindheimeri as a distinct species; older Central Texas sources commonly use C. capitatus var. lindheimeri.

evidence_basis: Travis — UT Plant Resources Center documents Croton capitatus var. lindheimeri, a current synonym of accepted C. lindheimeri.
Williamson — UT Vascular Plants of Williamson County documents C. capitatus var. lindheimeri; this is reconciled to current C. lindheimeri.
POWO and Flora of North America confirm Texas within the native range.

morphology.look_here_first: Ochraceous young pubescence, consistently acute leaf tips, and pistillate sepals whose tips stay straight to slightly incurved rather than recurving outward.
morphology.key_separator: Separates from true C. capitatus, whose pistillate sepals tend to flare/recurve after anthesis and which may show blunter/mucronate leaves.

photo_review.note: Current user-approved habit/fruit candidates are useful; a strong sepal-posture comparison with true C. capitatus remains the highest-value photo addition.
